claims.claim: The article's accepted interpretation is that Somatic Experiencing was developed to address inadequacies in prevailing cognitive/verbal/direct-exposure approaches as a complete account/treatment of trauma, while those approaches can still be useful.

support.primary_source: Payne P, Levine PA, Crane-Godreau MA. Somatic experiencing: using interoception and proprioception as core elements of trauma therapy. Front Psychol. 2015;6:93.
primary_source_points: SE is described as developed by Levine from 1977 onward.
SE's strategy is contrasted with primarily cognitive intervention and direct/intense exposure.
The paper calls a simple stimulus/response conditioning model inadequate for explaining complex behavior.
The paper identifies a drawback in talk therapy for trauma and describes the targeted regulatory system as relatively unaffected by rational thought.
The paper emphasizes interoception, proprioception, autonomic regulation, procedural memory, and completion of incomplete defensive responses.

claims.certainty: owner-accepted historical/causal interpretation supported by primary-source problem critique plus method design

claims.claim: Joel intentionally characterizes new cognitive-behavioral learning as suppressing old conditioned fear responses. This is an argumentative/theoretical characterization at the level of the article's contrast, not a claim that clinicians literally instruct patients not to feel and not a claim that every named therapy has one identical mechanism.

support.context: modern extinction/inhibitory-learning models support persistence of old fear associations alongside new learning that inhibits their expression
